headline: Amina is carrying 70.48 adjusted share against a circle mean of 62.67, and Farah is carrying 48.33, creating a deviation of 0.229 when the tolerance ceiling is 0.15.
what_i_tried: Built an opening split from stated availability and capacity
Moved four tasks from Amina to Rian to reduce Amina's load, but Rian's distance multiplied the weighted burden and reversed the imbalance
Moved those four in-person weekend tasks back to Amina to ease Rian's burden, but this pushed Amina's adjusted share to 96.13
Moved four tasks from Amina to Rian again to bring Amina down, landing at the current allocation
the_tension: Amina and Rian can trade tasks, but every in-person task carries heavy travel weight for Rian due to distance. Shifting weekend in-person work to Amina eases Rian but overloads Amina. Shifting it back to Rian eases Amina but crushes Rian. Farah cannot receive any of Amina's tasks because Farah has refused night shifts and is unavailable on Fridays and Saturdays, and the tasks that would rebalance the circle fall in those windows. The stated limits lock the three of you into a pattern where no task movement can bring everyone within tolerance of the mean.

options.label: Leave the allocation as it stands
options.consequence: Amina carries 70.48 adjusted share and Farah carries 48.33, with the deviation remaining above tolerance. Everyone has accepted their current schedule.

options.label: One sibling adjusts their stated availability or refusals to unlock new task paths
options.consequence: If Farah can take Friday or Saturday tasks, or accept night shifts, some of Amina's load can move. If Rian can accept weekday in-person work despite distance, some weighting pressure eases. If Amina can reduce declared capacity, the adjusted share calculation changes.

options.label: Reduce the total volume of tasks in the care plan
options.consequence: Fewer tasks may allow a fair split within everyone's stated limits, but this changes what care your mother receives.

what_i_will_not_decide: I will not choose between these because I do not know what any of you are carrying outside this plan, what your mother needs most, or what any sibling can truly afford to change. Those decisions belong to the three of you together.
